title: Context API — Sharing State Without Prop Drilling

subChunks.title: Context API — Sharing State Without Prop Drilling
subChunks.hookHtml: When state needs to reach deeply nested components — or be accessible from multiple unrelated parts of the component tree — passing it through props at every level becomes unmanageable. The Context API is React's built-in answer: define a value at one level, consume it anywhere below, with no manual prop passing in between.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Creating and providing context

import { createContext, useContext, useState } from 'react';

// 1. Create the context with a default value:
const ThemeContext = createContext('light');

// 2. Provide it in a parent component:
function ThemeProvider({ children }) {
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState('light');

  return (
    <ThemeContext.Provider value={{ theme, setTheme }}>
      {children}
    </ThemeContext.Provider>
  );
}

Consuming context

// 3. Any descendant reads the context with useContext:
function ToggleButton() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useContext(ThemeContext);

  return (
    <button onClick={() => setTheme(t => t === 'light' ? 'dark' : 'light')}>
      {theme === 'light' ? 'Switch to Dark' : 'Switch to Light'}
    </button>
  );
}

function ThemedCard({ children }) {
  const { theme } = useContext(ThemeContext);
  return <div className={`card card--${theme}`}>{children}</div>;
}

Custom hook for context

Wrap useContext in a custom hook for better error messages and ergonomics:

function useTheme() {
  const context = useContext(ThemeContext);
  if (!context) throw new Error('useTheme must be used inside ThemeProvider');
  return context;
}

// Usage:
const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();

Context and performance

When a context value changes, all consumers re-render — even those that only use part of the value. Mitigate this by:

  • Splitting contexts by concern (separate ThemeContext, AuthContext, CartContext)
  • Memoising the context value to prevent re-renders when the parent re-renders:
function CartProvider({ children }) {
  const [items, setItems] = useState([]);

  // ✅ Memoised value — only changes when items changes:
  const value = useMemo(() => ({ items, setItems }), [items]);

  return <CartContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CartContext.Provider>;
}

Vex: "Context solves prop drilling. It does not solve all state management problems. It is not a replacement for a proper state management library when you have complex cross-feature updates. Use it for: auth/user data, theme/locale, and feature-level shared state that is genuinely global within that feature."

When to use Context vs lifting state

Use Context when:

  • Data is needed by many components at different nesting levels
  • Prop drilling would cross 3+ levels
  • The data is truly shared and global within a feature or the whole app

Use lifting state when:

  • Only two or three sibling components need the same state
  • The relationship is clear and local

storyBeats.text: Vex strings a magical thread from the top of the tower to every room. 'Anyone can read the colour of this thread from anywhere in the building,' she says. 'No need to pass it through each room individually.'

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Context is a broadcast channel. The Provider shouts a value. Any component inside can listen with useContext. The catch: every listener re-renders when the value changes. Split your contexts by how often they change — auth state changes rarely, cart state changes often.

storyBeats.speaker: Provider + consumer pattern

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a theme system using Context:

  • Create a ThemeContext with a Provider that stores 'light' or 'dark'
  • Expose a useTheme() custom hook that reads the context
  • A <ThemeToggle /> component uses the hook to toggle the theme (data-testid="toggle")
  • A <ThemedBox children /> component applies className="box-light" or className="box-dark" based on context (data-testid="box")
  • Wrap everything in the Provider in the default export

guidedPracticeTests.label: Box starts with light theme class

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a CartContext system from scratch. The provider wraps the app and manages a cart (array of items). Expose: items, addItem(item), removeItem(id), total (derived). Create a useCart() hook. Use it in an AddToCartButton and a CartSummary component that displays item count and total. No scaffold.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain when to use Context vs lifting state. Give a concrete example of each. Why does Context cause all consumers to re-render when the value changes, and how do you mitigate this when you have a frequently-updated value like cart items?

questions.prompt: What happens when a Context value changes?
options: All components that consume that context with useContext re-render
React schedules a full app re-render
questions.answer: All components that consume that context with useContext re-render
questions.explanation: When the Provider's value prop changes, React re-renders every component in the tree that called useContext with that context. This is why splitting contexts by concern and memoising values matter — an auth context changing shouldn't re-render components that only care about theme.

questions.prompt: Why is wrapping useContext in a custom hook recommended?
options: It enables a descriptive error message when the hook is used outside its Provider, and provides a cleaner import/usage API
useContext cannot be called directly — it must be wrapped
Custom hooks cache the context value, improving performance
It prevents the context from triggering re-renders
questions.answer: It enables a descriptive error message when the hook is used outside its Provider, and provides a cleaner import/usage API
questions.explanation: function useTheme() { const ctx = useContext(ThemeContext); if (!ctx) throw new Error('useTheme must be inside ThemeProvider'); return ctx; } gives clear error messages instead of mysterious undefined errors. It also means consumers import useTheme, not both useContext and ThemeContext.

questions.prompt: A Provider's parent re-renders. The Provider's value is `{ user, setUser }` — an inline object. What happens?
options: All consumers re-render — a new object is created on every render, so the value always appears changed
Consumers only re-render if user actually changed
React deduplicates inline objects so consumers are not affected
The Provider prevents re-renders from passing through to consumers
questions.answer: All consumers re-render — a new object is created on every render, so the value always appears changed
questions.explanation: value={{ user, setUser }} creates a new object reference on every render of the Provider's parent. Shallow comparison sees a new object and triggers re-renders in all consumers. Fix: wrap the value in useMemo: const value = useMemo(() => ({ user, setUser }), [user]).
